comment: Represents the name or designation of the weather station.
World Meteorological Organization station identifier used to uniquely identify a weather station.
Represents the historical weather data product or category associated with the station.
Represents the complete local date and time of the weather data observation, providing more precision or granularity.
Represents the UTC (Coordinated Universal Time) date and time of the weather data observation in a string format.
Represents the latitude coordinate of the weather station's location in decimal degrees.
Represents the longitude coordinate of the weather station's location in decimal degrees.
Represents the observed or reported weather condition at the weather station.
Represents the ambient air temperature measured at the weather station, typically expressed in degrees Celsius.
Represents the perceived temperature adjusted for humidity and wind conditions.
Represents the dew point temperature, indicating the temperature at which air becomes saturated with moisture.
Represents the relative humidity, expressed as a percentage, indicating the amount of moisture in the air relative to the maximum it could hold at the same temperature.
Represents the temperature difference between two related temperature values, typically indicative of atmospheric instability.
Represents the visibility distance measured in kilometers, indicating how far objects can be seen clearly from the observation point.
Represents the observed wind direction at the weather station, typically expressed in degrees from true north.
Represents the wind speed measured in kilometers per hour.
Represents the wind speed measured in knots.
Represents the wind gust speed measured in kilometers per hour.
Represents the wind gust speed measured in knots.
Represents the atmospheric pressure at sea level adjusted using the barometric formula, measured in hectopascals (hPa).
Represents the atmospheric pressure reduced to mean sea level, typically used for weather analysis and forecasting.
Represents the trend or tendency of atmospheric pressure observed at the weather station, typically indicating whether it is rising, falling, or steady.
